title: Composite of compactifications: a compactification of p∘j with cartesian square
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}T$ morphisms of $S$-schemes whose structure morphisms to $S$ are separated, quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Let $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ be a compactification of $f$ and $c'=(Y\xrightarrow{j}Z'\xrightarrow{q}T)$ a compactification of $g$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Then the morphism $jp\colon Z\to Z'$ has a compactification $d=(Z\xrightarrow{i'}W\xrightarrow{p'}Z')$ whose square with sides $p$, $i'$, $j$, $p'$ is cartesian, i.e. $p'^{-1}(j(Y))=i'(Z)$ (take $W$ the scheme-theoretic closure of $Z$ in any compactification of $jp$). Consequently $X\xrightarrow{i'i}W\xrightarrow{qp'}T$ is a compactification of $gf$.

source.place: lem-sfb-localizing-lower-shriek-composition: composition Rg_! Rf_! = R(gf)_! uses a compactification of the composite whose square over the compactification of g is cartesian; Lean: upstream file lean/WeilConjectures/Compactification/Refinement.lean, declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Compactification.exists_isPullback_overG_overI (module WeilConjectures.Compactification.Refinement, lines 136-140, proof `sorry`)

proof.text: Use g.left ≫ T.hom = Y.hom and QuasiCompact.of_comp to obtain QuasiCompact g.left; T.hom is separated. Then c′.quasiCompact_openImmersion gives QuasiCompact c′.i. Properness of c′.g and qcqs of S imply CompactSpace c′.Z and QuasiSeparatedSpace c′.Z by applying QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace and quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated to c′.g ≫ T.hom.

The composite c.g ≫ c′.i is proper followed by an open immersion, hence separated and locally of finite type; it is quasi-compact by the preceding step and composition. Apply exists_isDense_compactification with target c′.Z, obtaining d and IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant d.i. Its open immersion is quasi-compact by d.quasiCompact_openImmersion.

Form d.restrict, the compactification of c.g on d.Z ×[c′.Z] Y.left, using Compactification.restrict in WeilConjectures.Compactification.Comp. Its open immersion t satisfies t ≫ pullback.fst d.g c′.i = d.i by restrict_i_fst, and the projection is a flat monomorphism. Since c.g is proper, d.restrict.isClosedImmersion_openImmersion makes t a closed immersion. Mathlib/source IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_comp gives schematic dominance of t from that of d.i and quasi-compactness of their composite. Thus t.ker_eq_bot and IsClosedImmersion.isIso_iff_ker_eq_bot make t an isomorphism. These are the explicit section-sheaf and closed-immersion steps of the proved private helper isIso_restrict_i_of_dense; no unproved witness or topological density substitute is used.

Transport d.isPullback_restrict across the inverse of asIso d.restrict.i, keeping the other three corners fixed. The two required equations follow from d.restrict.comm and restrict_i_fst. This gives IsPullback c.g d.i c′.i d.g in schemes. Lift it through Over.forget S by IsPullback.of_map, with the over-category commutativity supplied by Over.OverMorphism.ext d.comm. The witness d then has exactly the required square.

The consequent composite compactification in the node statement is already the existing overComp definition in this module: its open map is c.i ≫ d.i and proper map is d.g ≫ c′.g; their factorization equation is its existing comm proof. The theorem only asks for d and the cartesian square.
